model_status: source-checked parameters; partial historical numerical validation
source_edition: P1 G. J. Toomer, Ptolemy's Almagest; P2 O. Neugebauer, A History of Ancient Mathematical Astronomy (HAMA)

epoch.description: Nabonassar year 1, Egyptian Thoth 1, Alexandria mean local noon
epoch.calendar: Egyptian years of exactly 365 days; proleptic Julian correlation
epoch.time_scale: historical local mean days, not UT1 or TT

units.length: deferent-radius units, R=60; not physical distance
units.time: Alexandria mean local Egyptian day from Nabonassar epoch

mean_longitude_epoch.status: Almagest manuscript and IX.4 table reading
mean_longitude_epoch.source: P1 IX.4 p.427; XI.8 p.544 note; P2 HAMA p.182 n.15

unused_source_alternatives.meaning: epoch mean longitude from Ptolemy's stated back-computation
unused_source_alternatives.source: P1 XI.8 p.544 note; P2 HAMA p.182 n.15

unused_source_alternatives.meaning: later Handy Tables epoch mean longitude

source_discrepancies: P1 XI.8 p.544 note and P2 HAMA p.182 n.15 distinguish the Almagest manuscripts/IX.4 296;43, the stated calculation 296;44, and later Handy Tables 296;45. The Almagest model keeps 296;43.
P1 XI.7 p.543 note reconstructs the derived ancient anomaly as 183;16 rather than printed 183;17; the observation was used to infer a motion, not to test an independent prediction.
limitations: Exact continuous equant and epicycle geometry, not full original XI.11–12 correction-table interpolation.
Source-derived observations used to infer parameters are diagnostics, not independent predictive validation.
No latitude, physical distance, modern frame calibration or arbitrary-date observational accuracy claim.
